teams.heading: Fiji part ways with coach Mick Byrne eighteen months before World Cup
teams.body: Fiji Rugby ended Mick Byrne's tenure in April, with the Australian leaving "by mutual agreement" 18 months before the World Cup. Byrne had been in charge since 2024, after a stint at Fijian Drua, and his reign included wins over Scotland, Wales and Japan. AFP reported he appeared to have had a difference of opinion with management over future plans, and Fiji Rugby framed the move as necessary for the programme to follow its new direction.

lead.why: It is the only men's 15s story on the shortlist, and it is a named coaching change the reader has not seen on this tab.

teams.heading: Dupont, Ntamack and Ramos missed France's July opener against New Zealand
teams.body: Dupont, Ntamack, Ramos, Alldritt and Bielle-Biarrey were all missing from Fabien Galthié's squad for the July opener, the first Nations Championship test, against New Zealand in Christchurch. Many of the absences were put down to workload after the long Top 14 season, leaving a younger France group to face a formidable road opponent. The team's Nations Championship record now stands at two wins from three, including 42-15 over Japan in Round 3.

lead.why: The other candidates were already reported this week or were schedule and background pieces, so this July preview on France's missing stars is the strongest remaining item.

teams.heading: Bundee Aki’s latest ‘lippy’ outburst follows Connacht’s 36-19 Scotstoun mauling
teams.body: In the URC, Glasgow beat Connacht 36-19 at Scotstoun on Friday night, four of their five tries coming from the maul, and Planet Rugby’s round-three review leads with Bundee Aki’s latest ‘lippy’ outburst. Connacht, the Irish province, started the brighter but were reduced to 14 men by Sam Illo’s sin-binning before half-time, and last won away at Glasgow in September 2010.

lead.why: It is a new, men's club story that Irish fans will talk about, and it does not repeat the O'Sullivan pieces already run.

teams.heading: Italy go winless through three Nations Championship rounds, sitting 11th of 12
teams.body: Italy have no wins from three Nations Championship matches. In the log they sit 11th of 12, with no draws and three defeats. Across those three matches their points tally reads 37 for and 131 against, a difference of minus 94. The most recent result was a 10-57 loss to Australia in Round 3, and South Africa are next in Round 4.

teams.heading: World Rugby and UK bodies lose bid to dismiss brain injury claims
teams.body: The concussion litigation remains open, with the claimants facing a £2.8m legal bill to continue, as the Guardian reported earlier this week. The latest ruling reported came in late August: World Rugby and UK bodies lost a bid to have the brain injury cases thrown out of court. No coverage of a further move appeared in today's press, so the case stays open until the fees are settled or the claims resolved.

teams.heading: Koroibete set for Ospreys URC debut as Paea starts for Dragons
teams.body: In the United Rugby Championship (URC), Marika Koroibete makes his Ospreys debut on the wing at Rodney Parade, where the Wallabies star will look to help a side in search of its first win of the season after back-to-back defeats in South Africa. Facing them in the all-Welsh meeting, the Dragons come off a 38-26 win over Scarlets and make three changes to their starting XV, with Fetuli Paea starting at outside centre in his first start of the new season.

teams.heading: Mario Ledesma returns as Argentina forwards coach until 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Mario Ledesma is back in the Argentina set-up, taking charge of the forwards until the end of next year's World Cup in Australia, as the Union confirmed alongside Shaun Edwards' appointment. The 53-year-old former hooker played 84 Tests between 1996 and 2011 and was Argentina's head coach from 2018 to 2022. "I am honoured and very grateful for the opportunity to work with Los Pumas again," he said. Before this he worked as a consultant and at U17 level.

lead.why: The only NEW item in the shortlist, and it carries Mario Ledesma's return, the one part of the Argentina appointments not already covered in earlier editions.

teams.heading: Wallabies hold sixth in world rankings, just 0.11 clear of Scotland
teams.body: The Eden Park loss has cost the Wallabies ground in the World Rugby rankings. They drop from 85.55 to 84.89 points and hold sixth, just 0.11 clear of Scotland in seventh. Australia could have climbed to fourth, their highest ranking since November 2021, with a win by more than 15 points, but the 31-point defeat left them chasing. The All Blacks rose to 91.81, now just over a point behind South Africa on 93.09. Another defeat in Sydney on Saturday would see the Wallabies slip behind Scotland.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item that is genuinely new today; the other Bledisloe pieces repeat the Eden Park result or the Kiss quotes already published.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One reverses eligibility curbs after 24-player court settlement
teams.body: In August, Japan's domestic Rugby League One has rolled back a planned eligibility change after 24 affected players took the matter to court. Under the proposed rules, Japanese passport holders born abroad and not educated in Japan as children would have been restricted; the settlement treats players who acquired Japanese nationality before the end of May 2025 on a par with native-born players. Timothy Lafaele, who starred for Japan at the 2019 World Cup, was among the plaintiffs. Officials say the Japan-born pool is shrinking.

lead.why: It is the only shortlisted item not already reported and it concerns squad eligibility, a live integrity question for Japan's player pool, though it is older coverage.

teams.heading: All Blacks close to 1.28 points of Springboks in world rankings
teams.body: New Zealand's rating rose 0.66 after Saturday's 50-19 win over Australia at Eden Park, to 91.81, leaving them 1.28 behind South Africa on 93.09. The gap had been almost four points after the 3-1 series defeat to the Springboks. Planet Rugby reckons the All Blacks may fancy finishing the year as No. 1 if they come through next Saturday's Sydney Test unscathed.

lead.why: The world rankings race is a live competitive-status story that a fan would check, and it is not covered by the Bledisloe or injury editions already run.

teams.heading: Bulls thrash Lions 57-15 as returning Springboks Grobbelaar, Hanekom and Moodie shine
teams.body: Saturday's United Rugby Championship (URC) fixture, a club match rather than a Test, saw the Bulls beat the Lions 57-15 at Loftus Versfeld with four returning Springboks in the starting XV: Johan Grobbelaar, Gerhard Steenekamp, Cameron Hanekom and Canan Moodie. A yellow card to Lions scrum-half Morne van den Berg helped the hosts go 31-10 up at half-time. Handré Pollard came off the bench to slot three conversions, and the Bulls bounced back from a narrow defeat at Munster.

lead.why: A fresh result-based story from Saturday that puts four returning Springboks in the spotlight, unlike the rankings and ticket items already covered.
